title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Solutions of noble-metal precursors (e.g., chlorides/nitrates of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ir, Ru, Au, Ag) in coordinating solvents, sometimes pre-impregnated on carbon or confined in porous hosts.
recollection.intervention: Guess: A synchronized co-reduction route that equalizes reduction kinetics (e.g., ligand/halide-modulated borohydride or polyol reduction, potentially in a microfluidic or nanoconfined reactor) followed by rapid quenching to lock in targeted atomic ratios.
recollection.structure: Guess: Single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (~3–5 nm) with homogeneous, random atomic distributions across 5–7 noble metals, occasionally shape-controlled and/or supported on carbon.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Strong-ligand/halide mediation and high-supersaturation trigger near-simultaneous nucleation, suppressing sequential reduction and galvanic exchange; configurational entropy stabilizes a solid-solution HEA and prevents phase segregation during growth and post-synthesis handling.
recollection.results: Guess: Compositions matched to targets within about ±1–2 at% across a library of noble-metal HEAs; narrow size dispersity; improved electrocatalysis versus Pt/C (e.g., ORR mass activity on the order of 0.8–1.2 A mgPt−1 at 0.9 V with <10% loss after 20–30k cycles) and enhanced tolerance to poisons; robust structural homogeneity confirmed by STEM-EDS/atom mapping and single-phase XRD/PDF.

score.note: The recollection explicitly guesses an unrelated solution co-reduction/quenching method rather than spray-drying followed by H2 thermal decomposition-reduction. It generically identifies homogeneous single-phase HEAs, but incorrectly describes 3–5 nm fcc nanoparticles instead of porous 3D nanoframeworks with composition-dependent fcc/hcp phases. The ligand-mediated simultaneous-nucleation mechanism is wrong; the paper instead reports sequential noble-metal-assisted H2 reduction and a thermally activated fcc-to-hcp transition. All reported performance and composition numbers concern guessed ORR results and do not match the paper's MOR activity, ECSA, temperatures, or phase-transition values.
